metaDescription: MMSU Glut 2 corn is a glutinous open pollinated corn variety for the Visayas. About 98 days to harvest, 5.3 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: MMSU Glut 2 corn is a glutinous open pollinated corn variety, also sold or known as MMSU Glutinous 2. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2016 as NSIC 2016 Cn 308. It takes about 98 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain, with 5.33 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about MMSU Glut 2 corn
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

MMSU Glut 2 corn takes about 98 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. That is about the average of the 19 glutinous open pollinated corn varieties with a day count, 97.1 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 5.33 t/ha beats the average of its group, 5.09. One tonne of shelled corn fills about 20 sacks of 50 kilograms. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives 98 to 99 in national trials.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [Corn rust](/diseases/corn-rust), [Corn stalk rot](/diseases/corn-stalk-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm).

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn planthopper](/pests/corn-planthopper). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Its ears grew about 16.66 cm long in the trials. The shelling recovery was 75.56 percent, the share of the ear weight that comes off as grain. A higher share means more grain from every sack of ears. Against lodging it rated resistant, so it stood up well when wind and rain pushed the plants.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: shown with Glut 1 at MMSU's 2018 farmers' field day in Solsona, where farmers praised it as chichacorn. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant MMSU Glut 2 corn

It is recommended for the Visayas. Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items.q: Is MMSU Glutinous 2 the same as MMSU Glut 2?
items.a: Yes. MMSU Glutinous 2 is another name for MMSU Glut 2, registered as NSIC 2016 Cn 308. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 98 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 5.33 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.
It is recommended for the Visayas. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of MMSU Glut 2?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
